messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Planned transparent pool shuffle — 22 Aug 2026 (regional maintenance window)

Hi Jake and BrightLayer team,

Quick heads-up: we are scheduling a transparent "pool shuffle" across our us-east3 host pool this Sunday, 2026-08-22, between 23:00 and 01:30 PT (clock will show 2026-08-23 06:00–08:30 UTC). This operation is a rolling reallocation of hosts to apply a small driver/kmod update and rebalance long-running allocations.

What to expect:
- Rolling restarts of small subsets of hosts (max 8% of capacity at once).
- Short-lived connection migrations — most requests will continue; you may see 1–3 second latency blips during in-flight handoffs.
- Automatic fallback: requests routed to compatible model variants if affinity cannot be held.

Why we're doing this:
- Small driver compatibility fixes to reduce rare inference kernel panics observed under specific NIC firmware versions.
- Rebalancing to reduce instance hot-spots and improve tail latency long-term.

Action items for BrightLayer:
- No action required for most customers.
- If you must avoid any host reassignments during the window, you can opt out by submitting a short support request here: https://support.redwood.ai/requests/opt-out-maintenance — our ops team will schedule a pin for your tenancy and coordinate an alternative window.

Attachments: pool-schedule-2026-08.csv (regional staging), maintenance-fallback-playbook.pdf (what our on-call will execute).

We'll post real-time updates to our status page during the window: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-08-pool-shuffle

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Program Manager, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

--

Jake — good questions. Short answers below, followed by details.

1) Opt-out impact on reserved capacity: opting out will not change your subscribed reserved capacity numbers or baseline throughput guarantees. It may affect our ability to do immediate behind-the-scenes affinity optimizations for your tenancy, but we will coordinate a targeted maintenance window to perform the required updates with minimal impact to your SLAs.

2) Alternative window: yes — we can schedule an alternate maintenance window in the range you requested (02:00–06:00 PT) next Wednesday (2026-08-25). To request the alternate slot, please use: https://support.redwood.ai/requests/opt-out-maintenance and select the preferred window; our team will confirm within 4 business hours.

Details / Mitigations:
- When you opt out we create a temporary pin that prevents your host allocations from being selected for the shuffle; pinned nodes continue to receive updates via a staged path later.
- If you leave your tenancy in the regular shuffle, we will prioritize preserving KV cache where possible; we estimate cache re-warm of 10–15 minutes for large L2s in worst-case paths.
- We have a rollback path that the on-call will execute if we observe >1% request error spike or >200ms sustained p90 increase for more than 10 minutes. The rollback is captured in the attached maintenance-fallback-playbook.pdf.

Attachments included: maintenance-fallback-playbook.pdf (playbook), pool-schedule-2026-08.csv (per-region host groups).

If BrightLayer wants the alternate window, reply with preferred dates and we'll lock it in.

Best,
Priya

- Validate KV cache hit-rate delta for top 5 BrightLayer routes (compare T-24h baseline).
- Capture p50/p90/p99 for inference latency over the two-hour window post-maintenance.

- Sanity-check topology mapping to ensure pinned tenants were respected.

- We are attaching the internal validation snapshots to the runbook and have linked the status page incident: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-08-pool-shuffle

- We're planning a follow-up postmortem note that will summarize telemetry and any follow-through actions; ETA for that note is EOD Tue 2026-08-25.
